source: ដំណាំទុរេន (Durian Cultivation), Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries, Department of Agricultural Extension, 2015, 31pp
text: This source's pest coverage lists several insect groups affecting durian broadly consistent with Source A and Source B of this batch: fruit-boring caterpillars/moths that damage developing fruit from the inside; stem and twig borers (beetle larvae tunneling into wood); sap-sucking pests such as scale insects and psyllid-type insects on young shoots and flower clusters, which weaken new growth and can promote sooty mould through their honeydew excretion, similar in effect to the mealybug damage described in Source B. General control principles given are consistent across all three sources in this batch: regular monitoring, removing and destroying visibly infested plant material promptly, and targeted insecticide treatment at vulnerable growth stages (new flush, flowering, young fruit) rather than blanket spraying on a fixed schedule.
